OUR ANSWER IS THE ONE CONSISTENT WITH THE PRINTED REACTION. The stem's reaction is Zn(s) + Ag2O(s) + H2O(l) -> Zn2+(aq) + 2Ag(s) + 2OH-(aq), whose half-cells are anode Zn -> Zn2+ + 2e- (E = -0.76 V, Table 2.1) and cathode Ag2O + H2O + 2e- -> 2Ag + 2OH- (E = +0.342 V, standard), giving E(cell) = 0.342 + 0.762 = 1.104 V and DrG = -nFE = -213 kJ/mol. THE KEY'S NUMBER IS REPRODUCED EXACTLY BY A NAMEABLE SLIP: Table 2.1 prints Ag+/Ag = 0.80 and Zn2+/Zn = -0.76 (both verified at 6x zoom on p-06), and 0.80 - (-0.76) = 1.56 V to the digit. That substitutes the Ag+/Ag couple for the Ag2O/Ag couple — and there is no Ag+(aq) anywhere in the printed reaction. ROOT CAUSE, pre-registered blind by the authoring pass: the Ag2O/Ag couple is NOT in Table 2.1 and the chapter's own button-cell section describes the MERCURY cell (Zn-HgO, ~1.35 V), not the silver-oxide one, so the question supplies no data for its own cathode. COMPETING EXPLANATION, recorded honestly: a real silver-oxide button cell is ~1.55 V, but that voltage comes from an ALKALINE zinc anode (Zn/Zn(OH)2, about -1.25 V), which contradicts the stem's own Zn2+(aq) product. So under EITHER candidate mechanism the key's 1.56 V requires replacing one of the two printed half-reactions, while 1.104 V is the only value consistent with the reaction as written. The key also prints no DrG, so that half of the question is unkeyed. FOR MAINTAINER ADJUDICATION.
